extracted.intended_audience: Applicants seeking admission to the USPTO registration (patent bar) examination
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for submitting an application to sit for the USPTO registration (patent) examination, including required documents, fees, timelines, accommodations, and test administration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be complete for proper review by OED. It is strongly recommended that no incomplete application be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is incomplete if missing information in the form, fees, transcripts, or other required documentation. An incomplete application, if not timely completed, will result in denial of admission and require filing a new application and fees. Applicants are strongly encouraged to gather all information and documentation before submitting. See also 60-day completion period and notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on facsimile transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile transmissions of applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply online at the Exam Applicant Portal or send paper documents by mail/hand-delivery. Certificate of transmission and fax are not acceptable for registration applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file (submission methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking admission should apply online at the Exam Applicant Portal or send documents to Mailstop OED, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online filing is recommended. For hand delivery or courier services, obtain street address by calling OED. Include required documents and fees. Use the USPTO ID number on all subsequent correspondence once issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents (core checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include: a completed Application for Registration (Form PTO-158); the required application and examination fees; official transcripts; course descriptions (Category B only); all other required documentation (e.g., documents to show qualifications, evidence of permanent residence, or documents responding to questions 14–21); and, for aliens, copies of all documents submitted to/received from U.S. immigration authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness of each item before filing. Category B applicants must include course descriptions. Missing any of these items may render the application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and examination fees required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit the $118.00 non-refundable application fee and the $226.00 registration examination fee (and, if applicable, the $1,806.00 fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application and registration examination fee(s) may be paid with one check or credit card authorization. If paying the higher fee under §1.21(a)(10), $1,688.00 may be refundable only if not admitted. Failure to submit the appropriate fee may cause disapproval. Refund rules: $226 may be refunded to a disapproved applicant; $118 is not refundable. See regulation citations for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted payment methods and payment processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Government fees are payable in U.S. dollars by cashier's or certified check, Treasury note, or U.S. Postal Service money order; credit card payments are allowed but carry privacy considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments in other forms (including personal checks, credit cards or electronic funds transfer) may delay or cancel credit until collection is made. Do not send cash. There is a $54.00 processing charge for each refused payment or chargeback. A credit card form/instructions URL is provided. If credit card info is provided on non-official forms, Office is not liable if number becomes public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpayment and returned payment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If payment is refused by a financial institution (including returned checks or charged-back credit cards), the applicant will be refused admission or withdrawn if already admitted; passing the exam with unpaid fees results in denial of registration until fees paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants will be notified and given deadlines to pay outstanding amounts including processing fees under 37 CFR §1.21(m). Outstanding fees from prior applications block admission to future examinations until paid in full. Examples provided illustrating additional amounts owed for returned checks or prior unpaid fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper application signature and ink requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper application must be completed in permanent ink or computer (not pencil) and must be personally signed in accordance with 37 CFR § 1.4(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures must be original where required (e.g., petitions to OED Director require original signature). Facsimile transmissions not acceptable for signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and identification consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 1a: provide complete legal name (first, middle name not initial, last). Line 1b: provide name exactly as on current government-issued photo ID; same ID must be presented for admission to the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission will be denied if photo ID is expired or name differs from line 1b. At admission, Prometric will verify the ID/name provided on the admission letter which should match line 1b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact/address requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must enter the address where OED can communicate with the applicant during business hours (8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Eastern). If OED is to use a business address, provide business name/address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government employees must enter departmental name/address/telephone where employed rather than home address. If applicant wants notices at home, supply home address on separate sheet. Use USPTO ID number on all correspondence once issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical and immigration information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide citizenship (country), date of birth, place of birth, visa classification (if alien), permanent resident status (and submit copy of both sides of card if permanent resident), and alien registration number if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate immigration documentation where required. Failure to provide required immigration documents for aliens may render the application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee selection accuracy and related regulation compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should check the appropriate fee box on Line 8a and review 37 CFR §§ 11.7(h) and 11.7(k) to determine if the higher fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(10) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect fee submission may cause disapproval. If higher fee submitted but applicant fails to complete application or demonstrate qualifications, partial refund rules apply (refund less $118). Resubmission after adverse determinations may require resubmitting the higher fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former USPTO employee/waiver box
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 9: Check the box if applicant is a former patent examiner or other USPTO employee and seeks a waiver of the examination under 37 CFR § 11.7(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide relevant employment information to claim possible waiver eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior examination/registration disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines 10–13: disclose whether applicant previously passed the examination, previously applied for admission, prior registration to practice (include registration number), and bar membership in courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If attorney, upon passing must provide an original certificate of good standing bearing the seal of a state's highest court to be registered as a patent attorney. Do not submit certificate of good standing with application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral character and reputation disclosure duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines 14–21: Applicant must answer questions on moral character and reputation candidly and completely; any doubt should be resolved in favor of disclosure; duty to update responses in writing within 30 days of any change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or non-candid answers may lead to denial, revocation, or discipline (see 37 CFR §§11.7(a)(2)(i), 11.801, 11.804(c),(d)). Updates should reference the relevant application question and provide full details; failure to update may subject applicant to discipline and affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness guidance for disclosures (evidence and detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosing incidents in response to questions 14–21, applicant must provide a detailed statement with all relevant facts and dates and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete application would include: (a) full written explanation of incident details; (b) identification of law enforcement authority/jurisdiction; (c) statement of charges and disposition; (d) sanctions imposed and compliance explanation; (e) copies of documents/records and documentation of requests for them; (f) court records and documentation of requests; (g) for federal debt, records showing satisfaction or new payment arrangements and performance; (h) records showing sanctions and compliance. If unable to obtain documents, provide documentation of requests and any responses. Incomplete responses will be treated as incomplete application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of registration selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 22: check whether applying for registration for All Patent Matters or Design Patent Matters Only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct registration type to reflect intended practice scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 23: list all degrees and attach official transcripts for each degree and official course descriptions if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category B applicants must include course descriptions. Transcripts must be official; lack of transcripts will render application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to update application
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a continuing application; all information must be reported in writing and all changes (including address) must be signed, dated, and submitted within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes cannot be accepted by telephone, fax, or e-mail. See 37 CFR § 1.4(e) and 11.7(c) for timing. Applicants must continue to update until registered and should retain copies of all updates submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of payment specifics and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments must be in U.S. dollars and in specific forms; credit card payments require providing complete account number and expiration date; Office is not liable if credit card info provided on non-official forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official credit card form/instructions (URL provided). Returned or charged-back payments incur $54 processing charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines and processing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no filing deadline for the commercially administered computerized examination; applications are processed year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, incomplete applications not timely completed will be denied; fees filed with incomplete application will not be deferred or applied to the next application. Applicants are encouraged to file only complete applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application notice and cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: OED will notify applicant by letter if additional information or documentation is required and will indicate the extent to which the applicant meets or falls short of qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 60-day timeframe is provided to complete the application. Failure to respond within 60 days will result in disapproval. Replies to notices of incompleteness must be signed per 37 CFR §1.4(e). If the application remains incomplete after additional submissions, it will be disapproved and OED will provide a detailed explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing instructions and receipt confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPS mailing address and hand-delivery/courier procedures are specified; applicants may include a self-addressed, postage-paid postcard to request an acknowledgement of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED will stamp the postcard with the receipt date and mail it back, but the postcard is not verification that all identified items were present. Applicants should make and keep copies of every document submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact OED about application status
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not call OED regarding application status unless applicant has not received a response four weeks after submitting an application or papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no response four weeks after submission, contact OED as soon as possible thereafter. Extensions to take the examination may be requested in accordance with 37 CFR § 11.7(b)(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review of disapproval to OED Director
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with disapproval may petition the OED Director for review upon payment of the fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(5)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must bear original signature and be filed within 60 days of the notice of disapproval. The OED Director will review and issue a written decision which may grant admission or affirm the staff decision. If additional documentation submitted with petition is unsatisfactory, a final decision will be sent. Registration examination fee refunded in due course if disapproved; application fee not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: A final decision by the OED Director refusing admission may be reviewed upon petition to the USPTO Director under 37 CFR § 11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review requires filing a petition and payment of the fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(5)(ii) and must be filed within 30 days of the OED Director's final decision. Late petitions will be dismissed as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely-filing methods (mail/Certificate/Priority Mail Express)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods for timely filing replies or petitions: (i) First Class Mail or Hand-Delivery (date of receipt is date stamped); (ii) Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR § 1.8; (iii) Priority Mail Express® under 37 CFR § 1.10 (date-in on label is effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose method best suited for meeting deadlines. Certificate of transmission and facsimile are not acceptable. For hand delivery, documents received only during public hours (8:30 AM–5:00 PM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations request package
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request for Reasonable Accommodation package (Form PTO 158RA) consisting of an Applicant's Statement and a Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement must be completed to request accommodations for the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should check the box on PTO Form 158 that indicates the request is included. The completed package must be submitted with the Application Form 158 or separately addressed to Mail Stop OED. If an applicant is admitted, a separate notification of accommodations granted will be mailed. Contact OED for guidance if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations evidence and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide detailed responses in the Applicant's Statement and a completed Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement and/or other acceptable medical evidence to support the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide requested information may result in insufficient information to grant accommodation. After admission, scheduling with Prometric may take up to 30 days. If admission notice does not address the request, contact OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication for prior accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who received reasonable accommodations previously must submit a new Applicant's Statement with each new Application for Registration; depending on impairment, a new Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement may also be advisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency decisions are based on current impact of disability on the testing activity; for temporary or changing impairments, a current professional's statement may be required. For chronic conditions, a new statement may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination coverage and reference material
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination tests knowledge of applicable patent laws, rules and procedures, ability to analyze factual situations, and professional/ethical standards; questions are based on the MPEP and other published USPTO policy and procedure reference materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be familiar with patent statutes, USPTO rules of practice (Parts 1, 3, 11, 41, 42 of Title 37 CFR), the MPEP, and other published reference materials. Applicable laws/rules/policies control over MPEP in conflicts. OED will announce updated reference materials and which MPEP version is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination format and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination is 100 multiple-choice questions in two sessions: fifty questions in a three-hour morning session and fifty in a three-hour afternoon session (total of six hours). Each question has five choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A total of six hours is permitted. For commercially administered tests, reference materials will be available on the computer delivering the exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited items at the examination site
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not bring any documents, materials, machines, or electronic devices (including computers, telephones, recording devices, cameras, and typewriters) into the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For commercially administered examinations, reference materials will be on the computer and Prometric provides a storage locker for items not allowed in the testing area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination preparation materials and courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP and other reference materials are available on the USPTO website; the Office will not counsel applicants on statutes/rules nor recommend preparation courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot identify or recommend courses or offer advice as to special training required; applicants should use published materials for preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination results and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Official examination results will be released and mailed by OED. Commercially administered candidates will receive official results by mail soon after the exam. Candidates taking morning and afternoon sessions in a single day on a computer-delivered exam will receive unofficial results at the end of the examination on that computer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing candidates will receive instructions for completing registration at the time results are mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission letter and scheduling window
rubrics_metrics.description: After approval for admission, applicant will receive an admission letter with instructions to contact Prometric to schedule the exam within a specified window; the applicant must review the personal information on the admission letter for accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name on admission letter should match name on line 1b of application. Applicants should schedule promptly because test sites fill quickly. After the scheduling window expires, applicant must file a new application and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to scheduling window
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of the window for scheduling the examination are available for a fee of $124.00 under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(b)(4)(ii) and may be requested and granted an unlimited number of times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, request must be received before the current scheduling window expires and include the fee; if fee not included, request will not be granted. If request received after expiration, fee will be refunded. Prometric may charge separate scheduling/rescheduling fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prometric fee collection and scheduling process
rubrics_metrics.description: Prometric collects an examination administration fee from each candidate at time of scheduling; payment is due at scheduling and no fees are collected at testing centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants schedule directly with Prometric after OED approval. Prometric may provide three scheduling options: online, toll-free number, or local testing center contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prometric arrival, late, cancel, no-show, and reschedule policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should arrive 30 minutes early for check-in; arriving late will result in not being admitted. Late arrivals, reschedules, and no-shows are subject to Prometric policies. Failure to appear may forfeit fees and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescheduling via Prometric website or Prometric USPTO toll-free number. If a testing center cannot provide the exam on scheduled date (emergency/weather), the exam will be rescheduled to first available appointment at no additional charge. No-show may result in loss of eligibility at Prometric; if sufficient time remains in testing period, applicant may contact OED to reset eligibility; otherwise must reapply and pay fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required at testing center
rubrics_metrics.description: For admission to the commercially administered examination, an applicant must bring a current, valid State or Federal government issued ID (such as a driver's license or passport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ID must match the name on the admission letter/line 1b. Expired or mismatched ID may result in denied admission.
